papers.title: Sounding the Black Box: Online Training of Embedded Neural Networks in Forward-Only Physical Simulators
papers.summary: Hybrid physics-neural simulators embed neural networks in partial differential equation (PDE) solvers to model unresolved subgrid dynamics while preserving resolved physics and conservation laws. Because closure outputs feed back across time steps, single-step offline regression does not directly minimize multi-step rollout error, motivating online trajectory optimization. Solver backpropagation through time (BPTT) is the standard online solution when solver derivatives are available, yet many operational Fortran and C/C++ simulators expose only non-differentiable, forward-only interfaces. We introduce FORGE (Forward-Only Response and Gauss-Newton Estimation), an online framework that trains embedded networks from forward runs alone by decoupling exact network derivatives from black-box simulator dynamics. Stage I warms up the rollout via a low-dimensional Gauss-Newton step along output-orthonormal weight directions, canceling multi-layer feature drift via a final-layer correction. Stage II perturbs spatial output fields to fit a gain-bounded causal linear response operator across rollout steps, solves for regularized target outputs, and updates all weights via network backpropagation. Across five 2D and 3D benchmarks spanning phase separation, reaction-diffusion, fluid and MHD turbulence, and ocean circulation, FORGE outperforms gradient-free, reinforcement-learning, and emulator-based baselines, cutting coarse-solver test mean squared error (MSE) by 50%-96% in 2D and 70% in 3D, outperforming the strongest forward-only baseline by 16%-69%, and recovering 88%-98% of Solver BPTT's gains. Code is available at https://github.com/ChiyodaMomo01/FORGE.
papers.title_ja: ブラックボックスの音響：前方計算のみ可能な物理シミュレータにおける埋め込み型ニューラルネットワークのオンライン学習
papers.summary_ja: 微分方程式（PDE）ソルバに埋め込まれたニューラルネットワークを、勾配情報なし（前方計算のみ）の物理シミュレータ環境でオンライン学習するフレームワークFORGEを提案する。FORGEは、ガウス・ニュートン法による低次元ステップと、空間出力場の摂動を用いた因果線形応答演算子の推定を組み合わせることで、複数ステップのロールアウト誤差を最小化する。相分離、反応拡散、流体・MHD乱流、海洋循環などの2D/3Dベンチマークにおいて、勾配なし法や強化学習ベースラインを上回り、粗いソルバのテストMSEを50〜96%削減した。この手法は、微分不可能な既存のFortran/C++シミュレータでも高精度なサブグリッドスケールモデリングを可能にする。

papers.title: Automated Design and Evaluation Pipeline for Optimal Control Transcriptions in Model Predictive Control
papers.summary: The computational burden of Model Predictive Control represents a bottleneck limiting its widespread deployment in real-time applications. The selection of the optimal control transcription strategy for a given MPC formulation is a key driver of computational efficiency. Identifying performant MPC transcriptions requires significant effort and domain knowledge. We propose an automated pipeline for the design and evaluation of performant optimal control transcriptions for a given MPC formulation. Custom multi-objective design metrics, such as computation time or closed-loop performance, can be specified and are minimized by the pipeline. As a transcription method, a pseudospectral Legendre-Gauss-Radau method is employed. We show that it incorporates forward Euler integration and implicit collocation methods of low and high order in one formulation, leveraging the pipeline to evaluate both numerical approaches. Furthermore, different mesh configurations can be parameterized. To identify the optimal configuration of the transcription, a Bayesian Optimization framework is applied. The pipelines improvements in MPC performance are demonstrated through On-Orbit Servicing scenarios involving spacecraft motion planning and closed-loop control.
papers.title_ja: モデル予測制御における最適制御離散化手法の自動設計・評価パイプライン
papers.summary_ja: モデル予測制御（MPC）の計算負荷を軽減するため、最適制御離散化手法の自動設計と評価を行うパイプラインを提案する。疑似スペクトル法（Legendre-Gauss-Radau）を用い、前向きオイラー法や暗黙的配点法などの数値手法やメッシュ設定をパラメータ化して多目的最適化を行う。ベイズ最適化フレームワークにより、計算時間やクローズドループ性能などの指標に基づいて最適な構成を自動探索する。宇宙機の軌道計画と制御を含むオンオービットサービスシナリオにおいて、本手法がMPCの性能向上に寄与することを示した。

papers.title: Sampling at Scale: Distributed Multi-Agent Trajectory Optimization
papers.summary: Multi-agent trajectory optimization poses two coupled challenges: effectively exploring non-convex landscapes and scaling favorably to large teams of agents. Sampling-based methods are natural candidates for the exploration challenge but scale poorly with problem dimension. Moreover, their off-the-shelf integration into distributed optimization introduces a fundamental trade-off: sampling either fails to address the constraint-induced non-convexity or its search space grows with neighborhood size. We address this gap by introducing a $\underline{D}\text{istributed}$ $\underline{S}\text{ampling-based}$ $\underline{T}\text{rajectory}$ $\underline{O}\text{ptimization} \ \text{(DS-TO)}$ architecture built on a splitting mechanism tailored to sampling. Under this splitting, each agent samples only in its own control space, independent of neighborhood size, while still remaining exposed to both the constraint-induced non-convexity and the decisions of other agents. The resulting algorithm is fully decentralized, requiring only neighborhood communication, with all local updates executed in parallel across agents. Efficient variations, including parallel Jacobi updates within each agent's subproblem and single-step constraint linearization, further reduce computation. Experiments on 2D and 3D tasks with up to 1024 agents demonstrate improved exploration and constraint satisfaction over state-of-the-art derivative-based distributed optimization, and superior scalability to existing distributed sampling methods.
papers.title_ja: 大規模サンプリング：分散型マルチエージェント軌道最適化
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、非凸な探索と大規模エージェントへのスケーラビリティという2つの課題を持つマルチエージェント軌道最適化問題に対し、分散型サンプリングベースの軌道最適化（DS-TO）アーキテクチャを提案する。各エージェントが近傍サイズに依存せずに自身の制御空間のみでサンプリングを行う分割機構により、制約条件による非凸性と他エージェントの決定を同時に考慮しつつ、完全分散型で並列処理を実現する。2D・3Dタスクにおける最大1024エージェントの実験では、既存の微分ベース手法や分散サンプリング手法と比較して、探索効率と制約充足性、スケーラビリティの面で優れていることを示した。

papers.title: Learning Linear Time-Varying Koopman Models for Constrained Nonlinear Optimal Control
papers.summary: This paper presents a learning-based Koopman framework for solving constrained nonlinear optimal control problems. Despite significant advances in Koopman-based modeling and control, challenges remain in achieving accurate representations of controlled nonlinear dynamics and constraints while maintaining computational efficiency for optimal control. Motivated by these challenges, a linear time-varying (LTV) Koopman representation is developed to provide a more expressive representation of controlled nonlinear dynamics while preserving a linear prediction structure suitable for efficient convex optimization. Modeling errors and their propagation over extended prediction horizons are analyzed, motivating a neural-network-based Koopman framework that jointly learns lifted dynamics and constraint representations with stability-oriented regularization to improve long-horizon prediction performance. Based on the learned Koopman model, the original constrained nonlinear optimal control problem is reformulated as a convex quadratic program with conservative constraint tightening to account for modeling uncertainty during constraint enforcement. Numerical results on a low-thrust orbit transfer problem and a Mars entry guidance problem demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in terms of prediction accuracy, computational efficiency, and constrained optimal control performance.
papers.title_ja: 制約付き非線形最適制御のための線形時変コープマンモデルの学習
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、制約付き非線形最適制御問題を効率的に解くための学習ベースのコープマンフレームワークを提案する。制御された非線形ダイナミクスをより表現力豊かに記述しつつ、凸最適化に適した線形予測構造を維持する線形時変（LTV）コープマン表現を開発した。ニューラルネットワークを用いてリフトされたダイナミクスと制約表現を同時に学習し、安定性指向の正則化により長期予測時の誤差伝播を低減する。学習済みモデルに基づき、元の非線形問題を保守的な制約強化を伴う凸二次計画問題へ変換し、低推力軌道遷移や火星進入誘導の問題でその有効性を検証した。

papers.title: Space Postman and ATLAS: Enabling Startup Participation in the Orbital Logistics Economy
papers.summary: Debris removal, in-orbit servicing and refuelling, last-mile delivery, in-space recycling and constellation deployment are separate businesses built on one planning problem: a single spacecraft must visit many targets whose orbital planes drift apart under Earth's oblateness, within a propellant tank and a deadline. Solving it well takes orbital dynamics and optimisation expertise that is rarely the core business of payload, tug or constellation companies; this keeps young operators out of orbital logistics or leaves them with costly hand-made schedules. This paper presents Space Postman, a planning service that turns a target list, a spacecraft and a time budget into a priced and, for rendezvous tours, verified mission plan, and ATLAS, a tug concept whose payload bay takes debris kits, client spacecraft or propellant. As most start-ups fail when the money runs out, the offer starts with software and adds the vehicle later. Two case studies show what it changes. For a notional follow-on to the DEXTER project, which develops ways to turn scrap aluminium into propellant, it plans a tour of ten high-risk upper stages that share one orbital shell: waiting alone cannot close the tour, an even split of the time costs a third more propellant, and time is the currency of the mission. For a tug that releases eight clients from one rideshare, the delivery order decides whether the tank suffices, and the plan prices each delivery by the plane it must reach. The planning engine reproduces the published winning solution of a public debris-removal benchmark at that solution's fidelity and, given the same launches, plans cheaper trajectories for most of them: an independent check for operators and investors. A calibrated planner paired with a payload-agnostic tug offers new operators a practical way into orbital logistics, provided its numbers are read at the fidelity at which they were obtained.
papers.title_ja: Space Postman と ATLAS：軌道物流経済におけるスタートアップの参入を可能にする
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、軌道力学と最適化の専門知識を必要とする多目標訪問問題（TSP 類似）を解決する計画サービス「Space Postman」と、汎用トグコンセプト「ATLAS」を提案する。地球の扁率による軌道面ドリフトを考慮し、推進剤と時間制約下で効率的なミッション計画を生成する。DEXTER 後の高リスク段の回収や、ライドシェアからの複数顧客への配送といったケーススタディで、時間配分と訪問順序がコストに与える影響を実証する。さらに、公開されたデブリ除去ベンチマークの既存最良解を再現し、同等の発射条件下でより安価な軌道を計画できることを示すことで、手法の信頼性と実用性を検証している。

papers.title: Transferable, Time-Parallel Graph Dynamics via Space-Time Factorization
papers.summary: Time-parallel neural operators (FNO and successors) have transformed PDE surrogates on regular grids. Mesh-based operators (MeshGraphNets, Transolver) extend operator learning to irregular geometries, but jointly learning across diverse topologies while retaining non-recurrent temporal evaluation remains challenging. We propose space-time factorization: partition the model into local temporal operators (learned, graph-independent) and a spatial mixer that propagates information across nodes without graph-dependent learned parameters. This structural condition lets the same parameters run on unseen graphs; non-recurrent instances also admit time-parallel evaluation. Accurate zero-shot transfer further depends on controlling three information leaks (graph-dependent weights, graph-specific features, and graph-correlated training distributions) and on suitable task physics and training coverage. The protocol applies to two distinct spatial-mixer families, fixed-spectral and learned-attention. We validate the principle in three domains. For floodwave propagation in river networks, a 27K-parameter model trained on the Yangtze transfers zero-shot to the Mississippi with median NSE 0.998 in boundary-conditioned operational evaluation, training 5.5x faster than a stabilized recurrent baseline. On cross-geometry Navier-Stokes, the three-seed SepFNO mean relative vorticity error on five unseen targets falls by about 28% from 5 to 12 training geometries, with a consistent single-run SepTransolver trend. On cross-city traffic forecasting, zero-shot transfer reaches within 12.9% of an oracle trained on the target city. Across settings, cross-geometry error decreases with both the number of training geometries and their relatedness to the test, at a rate depending on the spatial mixer. This opens the path to pooled-data, foundation-style models for graph dynamics on irregular topologies.
papers.title_ja: 時空分解による移転可能で時間並列なグラフダイナミクス
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、不規則な幾何構造を持つグラフ上の物理現象を扱うニューラルオペレータにおいて、空間と時間の処理を分離する「時空分解」手法を提案する。グラフ依存のパラメータを空間ミキサーに限定し、時間演算子はグラフ非依存にすることで、未知のグラフ構造へのゼロショット移転と非再帰的な時間並列評価を両立させる。河川氾濫、ナビエ・ストークス方程式、交通予測の3領域で検証し、特に河川ネットワークでは訓練済みモデルが別の河川にゼロショット移転して高精度を維持し、再帰型ベースラインより5.5倍高速に訓練できることを示した。この手法は、不規則トポロジー上のグラフダイナミクスにおける基盤モデル構築への道を開くものである。
papers.relevance_reason: サロゲートモデルと物理情報ニューラルネットの高速化・移転可能性に直結

papers.title: Diagnosing Epistemic Uncertainty in Neural Operators: Effects of Initialization, Discretization, and Function Sampling
papers.summary: Neural operators provide efficient surrogates for mappings between function spaces, but their reliability cannot be characterized by the performance of a single trained model. Existing neural operator uncertainty quantification approaches often characterize predictive uncertainty without separately identifying the contributions of individual sources of epistemic uncertainty. Finite sampling of the training function space, output discretization, and model initialization can produce substantial variation among learned operators even when the underlying physical problem is deterministic. We systematically investigate these sources of epistemic uncertainty across a diverse set of operator learning architectures. Across our experiments, we train approximately 46,000 neural operator models and construct ensembles over training datasets, model initializations, and output discretizations to characterize distributions of relative $L_2$ error rather than individual trained realizations. We find substantial architecture-dependent differences in epistemic uncertainty, with model initialization often accounting for the largest proportion of variance in relative $L_2$ error. The ranked performance of neural operator architectures can invert as the number and spatial distribution of output samples change, with the best architectures under sparse or randomly sampled observations differing from those at higher-resolution or structured discretizations. Furthermore, ensembles that reliably characterize aggregate operator error can provide unreliable estimates of error quantiles for individual test functions. These results highlight the importance of distinguishing the sources of epistemic uncertainty when evaluating neural operator reliability and establishing robust benchmarking practices.
papers.title_ja: ニューラルオペレータにおける認識的不確実性の診断：初期化、離散化、関数サンプリングの影響
papers.summary_ja: ニューラルオペレータの信頼性を評価するため、初期化・離散化・関数サンプリングによる認識的不確実性の寄与を体系的に調査した。約46,000個のモデルを訓練し、相対L2誤差の分布をアンサンブルで特徴づけた結果、初期化が誤差分散の最大要因であることが判明した。また、出力サンプルの密度や分布によってアーキテクチャ間の性能順位が逆転する現象も確認された。個々のテスト関数に対する誤差量子の推定が不安定になる場合もあるため、不確実性の源を区別した堅牢なベンチマーク手法の重要性が示唆される。
papers.relevance_reason: ニューラルオペレータの不確実性評価とベンチマーク設計は、ユーザーの関心であるサロゲートモデルと評価手法の交点に位置する。

papers.title: Multi-agent System for Automatic Discovery of Pareto-optimal Meta-solvers for PDEs
papers.summary: Designing linear solvers for discretized partial differential equations requires problem-specific expertise. We present a multi-agent framework, in which language-model agents propose, critique, implement, and evaluate solver configurations assembled from Krylov methods, preconditioners, block factorizations, and neural operators. Inside the proposing agent, a non-dominated sorting genetic evolutionary algorithm evolves the population of meta-solvers toward the Pareto front of six measured quantities, so that one run returns a front of trade-offs rather than a single tuned solver. The system runs on small open-weight language models served on a single laptop, and we compare it with a single agent on four problems. For three-dimensional acoustic scattering and elasticity, it delivers 47 and 48 convergent hybrid solvers out of 60 candidates. Relative to the Jacobi-preconditioned Krylov baselines, the best of the discovered solvers reduce the iteration counts by factors of 4.7 and 60 and the online solve time by factors of 2.3 and 3.0, whereas the single agent produces no executable plan. For coupled dynamic thermoelasticity in two and three dimensions, where the baselines fail, it completes 98 of 100 transient candidates and, compared with the single agent, reaches a given accuracy 15 times faster in two dimensions and a displacement error 20 times lower in three dimensions.
papers.title_ja: PDEのパーレート最適メタソルバーの自動発見のためのマルチエージェントシステム
papers.summary_ja: 離散化偏微分方程式（PDE）の線形ソルバー設計において、言語モデルエージェントがKrylov法やニューラルオペレータを組み合わせた構成を提案・評価するマルチエージェントフレームワークを提案する。提案エージェント内部では、非支配ソート遺伝的アルゴリズムを用いて6つの指標に対するパーレートフロンティアを探索し、単一の最適解ではなくトレードオフの集合を返す。小型オープンウェイトLLMを単一ラップトップ上で動作させ、音響散乱や弾性問題においてベースライン比で反復回数を最大60倍、オンライン計算時間を3.0倍削減するハイブリッドソルバーを発見した。また、結合動的熱弾性問題ではベースラインが失敗するケースでも高効率な解を生成し、単一エージェントと比較して精度達成速度や誤差において大幅な性能向上を示した。

papers.title: SPARK: Spectral Preconditioned Analytic Residual Kolmogorov Arnold Networks for incompressible Navier Stokes equations
papers.summary: We propose Spectral Jet KAN (SJ-KAN) to reduce the cost of differentiation and the network complexity of Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) for the Navier-Stokes (NS) equations. The input coordinates are embedded through Chebyshev bases whose spatial derivatives are known in closed form, and all differentiation matrices are computed once for the collocation points before training. A single linear layer compresses the Chebyshev bases into a few latent features, and a single nonlinear Chebyshev Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (CKAN) layer maps these features to the physical variables. Because the basis derivatives are known in advance and the compression is linear, the spatial derivatives in the NS equations are carried through the network analytically by a fixed sequence of matrix products and elementwise operations. Automatic differentiation (AD) is used only in backpropagation, to compute the gradients of the loss with respect to the network weights. We examine three variants of SJ-KAN (JetKAN, JetKAN-F, JetKAN-H), which differ in how the output layer maps the latent features to the physical variables. All variants are tested on the Taylor-Green vortex and on the lid driven cavity at Reynolds numbers Re = 100, 1000, 5000 and 10,000. The results are compared with a KAN that uses AD (PIKAN) and with a standard PINN. The SJ-KAN variants reach comparable or better accuracy than both, with up to 47 times fewer parameters and up to 8.2 times faster training per epoch. SJ-KAN also solves the lid driven cavity flow at Re = 10,000 without any reference data and with fewer than 9,000 trainable parameters. These results show that analytic derivative propagation, a small spectral input layer and a single KAN layer give a faster and simpler solver than methods based on AD, also for flows at high Reynolds numbers.
papers.title_ja: SPARK: 非圧縮性ナビエ・ストークス方程式のためのスペクトル事前条件付き解析的残差コルモゴロフ・アーノルドネットワーク
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、ナビエ・ストークス方程式を解く物理情報ニューラルネットワーク（PINN）の計算コストと複雑さを削減するSJ-KANを提案する。チェビシェフ基底を用いて空間微分を解析的に処理し、自動微分（AD）の負荷を軽減する。Taylor-Green渦やリッド駆動キャビティ流のシミュレーションにおいて、既存手法と比較し、パラメータ数を最大47分の1、訓練速度を最大8.2倍高速化しながら同等以上の精度を達成した。高レイノルズ数流においても参照データなしで高精度な解を得ることを示し、効率的なサロゲートモデルとしての有効性を証明している。

papers.title: Physics-informed neural networks for strong normal shocks in kinetic relaxation models and the hard-sphere Boltzmann equation
papers.summary: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) for kinetic equations have mostly been applied near equilibrium and judged by density, velocity and temperature. Here a network trained on the kinetic equation alone, with no reference data in the loss, solves steady normal shock waves and is assessed in eight fields: density, velocity, temperature, heat flux, stress, a third-order moment and two fourth-order moments. The network corrects a mixture of the two end-state Maxwellians by an unbounded, signed factor with exact inflow; the loss, the residual in three norms with conservation terms, is minimised by Adam and a self-scaled quasi-Newton method with continuation in the Mach number. For the hard-sphere Boltzmann equation at Mach 8, in a comparison made once after reference-free tests, the largest relative $L^2$ difference from direct simulation Monte Carlo (DSMC) over the eight fields is 0.19 per cent; at Mach 10 it is 0.34 per cent. The distribution function itself agrees with the reference over six decades in velocity space. For the Bhatnagar--Gross--Krook (BGK) model, a blind prediction at Mach 50 gives density, velocity and temperature to about 0.1 per cent and exposes a loss of accuracy confined to the two fourth-order moments. Its origin is identified as a passive reduced distribution that carries little weight in the loss; with a larger weight on that distribution and a longer optimisation, both moments are within 3.2 per cent of the discrete-velocity solution up to Mach 70 and 7.1 per cent at Mach 100. The Shakhov model is solved to Mach 20 and a Rykov-type model of nitrogen to Mach 15.
papers.title_ja: 運動論的緩和モデルおよび硬球ボルツマン方程式における強い正激波に対する物理情報ニューラルネットワーク
papers.summary_ja: 本研究は、参照データを用いずに運動論方程式のみから学習する物理情報ニューラルネットワーク（PINN）を提案し、強い正激波の定常解を高精度に予測する手法を提示する。硬球ボルツマン方程式においてマッハ数8〜10でDSMC法との誤差が0.19〜0.34%と極めて小さく、分布関数も速度空間6桁にわたり一致した。BGKモデルでは高マッハ数域での高次モーメントの精度低下を特定し、損失関数の重み調整によりマッハ数100まで3.2%以内の精度を達成した。
papers.relevance_reason: PINNと物理方程式の統合、高次モーメントの精度改善というユーザー関心と高度に一致

papers.title: CoMNO: Commutator Memory Neural Operators for Long-Horizon PDE Prediction
papers.summary: Solving nonlinear partial differential equations (PDEs) over long time horizons is computationally expensive using traditional numerical methods. While neural operators provide an efficient alternative, they suffer from the accumulation of approximation errors along the predicted trajectory, typically caused by the failure to capture fine-scale details. In this work, we design a Commutator Memory Neural Operator that identifies fine-scale dynamical details by commuting two operations and leverages these details to enhance the neural operator's capability in capturing fine-scale features over long time horizons. Specifically, we identify a performance gap between two operations: downsampling the high-resolution field before rollout prediction versus performing rollout prediction before downsampling. We observe that fine-scale dynamical details are often encoded in this gap. By commuting these two operations, the fine-scale details removed during downsampling can be captured. Furthermore, we employ a memory module to store these fine-scale features along the trajectory and retrieve them during rollout, generating spatially adaptive corrections that enhance long-horizon fidelity. Empirical results across five systems demonstrate that CoMNO improves prediction accuracy and long-horizon rollout stability.
papers.title_ja: CoMNO: 長時間PDE予測のための交換子メモリニューラルオペレータ
papers.summary_ja: 非線形偏微分方程式（PDE）の長時間予測において、従来の数値手法は計算コストが高く、既存のニューラルオペレータは誤差蓄積により精度が低下する問題がある。本論文では、ダウンサンプリングとロールアウト予測の順序を入れ替えることで生じる「交換子」から微細な動的詳細を抽出する手法を提案する。この微細特徴をメモリモジュールに保存し、予測時に空間的に適応的な補正として活用することで、長時間の軌道予測における安定性と精度を向上させる。5つの物理系での実験により、従来の手法を上回る予測性能を実証した。
papers.relevance_reason: ニューラルオペレータと長時間予測の高速化・精度向上に直結する手法

papers.title: Contract2Reach: Discretization-Induced Contractive Dynamic Programming for High-Dimensional Hamilton-Jacobi Reachability
papers.summary: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) enable undiscounted Hamilton-Jacobi (HJ) reachability analysis for high-dimensional systems, but their performance can be sensitive to hyperparameter choices and the underlying system dynamics. We introduce Contract2Reach, which recasts undiscounted finite-horizon reachability as a sequence of contractive fixed-point problems solved by backward time marching. Our formulation combines discretized temporal and spatial derivatives to construct a contractive mapping without introducing a discount factor. Under standard assumptions, we prove that the exact scheme converges to the unique viscosity solution as both the temporal and spatial step sizes tend to zero. Unlike PINNs, our training fits rollout-based value targets via a single regression, without backpropagating through spatial value gradients. In the neural implementation, adaptive zero-level-set sampling and conservative target combination address high-dimensional sample sparsity and false positives, respectively. Experiments on a parameterized vertical drone, a 13D quadrotor, and a 40D publisher-subscriber system show competitive performance against PINNs-based baselines. Boundary evaluations on the vertical drone and publisher-subscriber systems demonstrate improved fidelity and reduced learning-rate sensitivity, revealing errors that volume-based metrics can miss.
papers.title_ja: Contract2Reach: 高次元ハミルトン・ヤコビ到達可能性解析のための離散化誘起収縮型動的計画法
papers.summary_ja: 高次元システムにおけるハミルトン・ヤコビ（HJ）到達可能性解析において、物理情報ニューラルネット（PINN）のハイパーパラメータ依存性や収束性の問題を解決する手法を提案する。本手法は、割引係数なしの有限時間到達可能性を、時間逆方向マーチングによる収縮型固定点問題の連立として定式化し、厳密なスキームが粘性解に収束することを証明する。学習は空間勾配を通じた逆伝播を避け、ロールアウトベースの価値ターゲットへの単一回帰により行い、適応的なゼロレベルセットサンプリングと保守的なターゲット結合により高次元でのスパース性と誤検出を抑制する。13次元クアッドローターや40次元システムでの実験により、PINNベースのベースラインと比較して競合する性能と、学習率への感受性の低減、および境界評価における精度向上を実証した。
papers.relevance_reason: PINNと高次元最適化・軌道設計の高速化に直結する手法

papers.title: Learning Inelastic Homogenization with Memory: Deep Material Networks and Discrete Adjoints
papers.summary: Deep material networks (DMNs) provide mechanically structured surrogate models for computational homogenization. Traditionally, they are identified from elastic data and subsequently extrapolated to inelastic responses. This procedure leverages highly efficient linear solvers and provides robust extrapolation to different inelastic constitutive laws. However, selecting the appropriate linear elastic training data for a given inelastic constitutive behavior is non-trivial. In this work, we identify the DMNs directly from macroscopic stress-strain trajectories. Applying automatic differentiation to such problems with history entails a huge memory demand, excluding most practically relevant problems. To mitigate, we derive a path-consistent discrete adjoint that avoids propagating parameter-wise state sensitivities by treating equilibrium and internal variable evolution over the complete loading history as coupled constraints. For a short-fiber composite with an elastoplastic matrix, the adjoint approach reproduces the sensitivities obtained by direct differentiation and by an independent automatic-differentiation implementation, while it requires only one backward solve of the linearized state equations per time step and avoids the parameter-wise propagation of state sensitivities. Inelastic training also improves predictive accuracy: A rank-$5$ DMN trained on inelastic trajectories outperforms a deeper rank-$8$ DMN trained on elastic homogenization data for different loading paths. This advantage is retained under perturbations of the constituent inelastic material parameters. The resulting inelastic trained DMNs preserve the same formulation for online deployment and remain several orders of magnitude faster than the full-field homogenization solver.
papers.title_ja: 記憶を持つ非弾性均質化の学習：ディープマテリアルネットワークと離散アジュoint
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、計算均質化におけるサロゲートモデルであるディープマテリアルネットワーク（DMN）の非弾性挙動への適用を提案する。履歴依存問題における自動微分のメモリ負荷を軽減するため、パラメータ毎の状態感度伝播を回避するパス整合型離散アジュoint法を導出する。短繊維複合材の弾性塑性マトリックスに対し、この手法が直接微分や独立した自動微分と同等の感度を再現しつつ、計算コストを大幅に削減することを示す。非弾性軌跡で訓練した低ランクDMNは、弾性データで訓練した高ランクDMNよりも予測精度が高く、フルフィールドソルバーより桁違いに高速なオンライン推論を実現する。
papers.relevance_reason: サロゲートモデルと物理情報手法、および計算高速化の核となる手法

papers.title: RECAP: Training Long-horizon LLM Agents with Context Compaction
papers.summary: Context compaction enables large language model agents to tackle long-horizon tasks within limited context budgets by replacing interaction histories with compressed summaries. However, learning effective compaction jointly with the agent policy remains challenging, as summaries affect task success over many subsequent interactions. We introduce RECAP, a reinforcement learning (RL) framework based on the principle that a summary should preserve the behavior induced by the original interaction history. We formalize this principle with a behavior distortion objective that measures the divergence between the agent's subsequent behavior under compressed and original contexts. We show that the gradient of the distortion objective decomposes into two complementary learning signals: distortion-based reward for summary generation and self-distillation for subsequent actions. Experiments on Qwen3.5-4B show that RECAP consistently outperforms the task-reward-only RL baselines on both environments, leading to an absolute improvement of 4.6% and 4.3% on BrowseComp-plus and SWE-bench Verified, respectively. Ablations further highlight the value of jointly supervising summary generation and post-compaction behavior for RECAP.
papers.title_ja: RECAP: コンテキスト圧縮を用いた長期LLMエージェントの学習
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、コンテキスト予算内で長期タスクを遂行するためのLLMエージェント向けコンテキスト圧縮手法RECAPを提案する。要約が元の対話履歴から誘起されるエージェントの行動を保持すべきという原則に基づき、圧縮前後の行動分布の乖離を測る「行動歪み目的関数」を定式化する。この勾配を分解することで、要約生成への報酬信号と後続アクションへの自己蒸留という2つの補完的な学習シグナルを導出する。Qwen3.5-4Bを用いた実験では、タスク報酬のみを用いた強化学習ベースラインと比較し、BrowseComp-plusとSWE-bench Verifiedでそれぞれ4.6%、4.3%の絶対向上を示した。
papers.relevance_reason: LLMエージェント設計と強化学習の融合であり、ユーザーの関心領域に直結する。

papers.title: SD-Cache: Learnable Memory Consolidation with State-Guided Dynamic Caching
papers.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as persistent services that must reason over large volumes of external knowledge. Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) grounds model responses in relevant documents, but the retrieved content must still be encoded and stored in the key-value (KV) cache. As this content accumulates, the cache grows linearly, increasing memory consumption and inference cost. Existing memory-compression methods address this problem either by retaining a subset of cached states or by learning context compressors that map documents to compact latent representations. Despite these advances, consolidating information under tight memory budgets while preserving its usefulness for future queries remains challenging. We investigate how the model's native KV states can be selectively consolidated into a fixed-size working memory without access to future queries. To this end, we introduce SD-Cache (State-guided and Dynamically updated Cache), a query-agnostic KV-memory consolidation framework that operates alongside a frozen generator LLM. SD-Cache learns to consolidate layer-wise KV states into fixed-size memory through selective anchor-based pooling and state-guided refinement, processing new contexts in a single forward pass without context-specific optimisation. Experiments on retrieval-augmented question answering and synthetic long-context benchmarks show that SD-Cache maintains competitive downstream performance under constrained memory budgets.
papers.title_ja: SD-Cache: 状態誘導型動的キャッシュによる学習可能なメモリ統合
papers.summary_ja: 大規模言語モデル（LLM）の推論時におけるKVキャッシュのメモリ肥大化問題を解決するため、固定サイズのワーキングメモリへ情報を統合するフレームワーク「SD-Cache」を提案する。本手法は、将来のクエリに依存せず、レイヤーごとのKV状態を選択的アンカーベースプーリングと状態誘導型リファインメントにより圧縮する。凍結された生成器LLMと併用し、新しいコンテキストを単一フォワードパスで処理することで、メモリ制約下でも競争力のある下流タスク性能を維持することを示した。
papers.relevance_reason: LLM推論高速化・メモリ効率化とRAG設計の両方に直結する重要手法

papers.title: Learning What vs. Learning How: Decomposing Task and Interface Competence in Agentic Training
papers.summary: LLM agents operate through harnesses that define system prompts, action formats, feedback loops, and resource constraints. A model may possess the knowledge needed to solve a task yet fail to express that knowledge through a particular harness. This raises a basic question: when a policy fails under a given harness, is it missing task knowledge or the competence to operate the interface? We distinguish two components of agentic competence: task competence, the knowledge and reasoning needed to solve a task, and interface competence, the ability to act on that knowledge through a given harness. Across four reasoning and agentic benchmarks, we show that harness-conditioned training yields vastly different outcomes depending on how these interact. Multi-harness distillation aggregates task knowledge from trajectories collected through different harnesses into a shared policy, but this knowledge is realised only when training preserves or improves competence on the inference-time interface. Otherwise, single-harness training can induce interference in interface competence, sometimes catastrophically collapsing performance on a held-out harness despite improvements in underlying task knowledge. To disentangle task and interface supervision, we introduce harness rehearsal: distillation on traces that carry minimal task knowledge while exercising the target interface. Cross-harness task supervision or rehearsal alone yields little gain, but their combination yields gains far larger than either: on BFCL V3 multi-turn with Qwen3-4B, they achieve 8.5% and 32.5% respectively, versus 58.8% together. Finally, on-policy reinforcement learning (RL) is more robust than distillation to single-harness training: it does not substantially degrade performance on other harnesses, and interface competence acquired through multi-harness distillation persists through subsequent RL.
papers.title_ja: 何を学ぶか vs. どのように学ぶか：エージェント訓練におけるタスク能力とインターフェース能力の分解
papers.summary_ja: LLMエージェントの性能は、タスク解決に必要な知識（タスク能力）と、特定のハーネス（プロンプトやアクション形式など）を通じて行動する能力（インターフェース能力）の両方に依存する。本研究では、これらを分離し、マルチハーネス蒸留と「ハーネスリハーサル」（最小限のタスク知識でインターフェースを訓練する手法）を組み合わせることで、単一ハーネス訓練による干渉や性能崩壊を回避し、大幅な性能向上を実現することを示した。さらに、オンポリシー強化学習は蒸留よりも単一ハーネス訓練への耐性が強く、獲得したインターフェース能力が維持されることも確認された。
papers.relevance_reason: LLMエージェント設計と強化学習の最適化に直結する手法

papers.title: SwiftLoop: Selective Refinement for Adaptive Implicit Reasoning in Looped Transformers
papers.summary: Looped Transformers advance implicit chain-of-thought reasoning through recurrent latent refinement. However, existing looped reasoners typically employ fixed-depth recurrence, updating all latent positions at every iteration and incurring redundancy when further refinement is unnecessary. We introduce \textsc{SwiftLoop}, an inference-time framework for selective recurrent refinement through position-wise freezing, enabling adaptive computation allocation across both recurrent depth and active width. SwiftLoop learns lightweight freezing policies through hindsight-guided supervision derived from two complementary criteria: K/V reusability at the internal representation level and functional impact at the output level. At inference time, these policies guide adaptive freezing based on observed hidden states. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SwiftLoop achieves favorable accuracy--computation trade-offs over fixed-loop inference and adaptive baselines, with measured inference acceleration. Beyond implicit reasoning, we further demonstrate its applicability to recurrent prompt prefilling in general looped models.
papers.title_ja: SwiftLoop: ループ型Transformerにおける適応的暗黙推論のための選択的洗練
papers.summary_ja: ループ型Transformerの暗黙的推論において、固定深度の反復計算による冗長性を解消する推論時フレームワーク「SwiftLoop」を提案する。内部表現のK/V再利用可能性と出力への機能的影響を基準とした事後監督により、位置ごとの凍結ポリシーを学習し、計算資源を適応的に配分する。実験により、固定ループ推論や適応ベースラインと比較して精度と計算量のトレードオフが優れ、推論速度の向上が実証された。また、一般的なループ型モデルにおけるプロンプトプリフィルリングへの適用可能性も示されている。
papers.relevance_reason: LLM推論高速化・効率化の核心手法であり、ユーザー関心と高度に一致

papers.title: Collision Rendering: GPU-Accelerated Trajectory Planning on Sparse Voxel Radiance Fields with Risk-Bounded Collision Checking
papers.summary: Although radiance fields provide detailed scene representations for robotics, they remain underexplored for trajectory planning, without a widely agreed-upon way to translate learned spatial primitives into reliable collision criteria. To bridge this gap, we introduce Collision Rendering, the first trajectory planning framework on sparse voxel radiance fields (SVR), which supports GPU-accelerated, risk-bounded collision checking and a differentiable collision cost. Our key insight is that the structured volumetric density of SVR allows its rendering pipeline to serve as a fast numerical approximator of collision probability. We approximate the robot with collision spheres and place a coinciding spherical camera at each sphere. Under a probabilistic collision model, we derive an upper bound on each sphere's maximum directional collision probability from the camera's rendering pipeline. Evaluating this bound on the GPU yields a modular collision checker that integrates with established sampling-based planners without an auxiliary geometric map or changes to the learned representation. We further compute a collision cost and its gradients from rendered opacities through the same pipeline, extending the framework to trajectory optimization. Experiments demonstrate millisecond collision checking time on a consumer-grade GPU and collision-free trajectories in all queries, outperforming other radiance field-based planners.
papers.title_ja: Collision Rendering: 疎ボクセル放射場におけるGPU加速軌道計画とリスク限界付き衝突チェック
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、疎ボクセル放射場（SVR）を用いたロボットの軌道計画フレームワーク「Collision Rendering」を提案する。SVRのレンダリングパイプラインを衝突確率の高速数値近似器として活用し、GPU上でミリ秒単位のリスク限界付き衝突チェックを実現した。さらに、レンダリングされた不透明度から微分可能な衝突コストを導出することで、既存のサンプリングベースプランナーや軌道最適化アルゴリズムとシームレスに統合可能である。実験により、消費者向けGPU上で他の放射場ベースのプランナーを上回る性能と、全クエリでの衝突回避能力が示された。
papers.relevance_reason: 軌道計画・最適化とGPU加速・深層学習表現の融合であり、ユーザーの関心領域に強く該当する。

papers.title: Aerodynamic Collision Avoidance Manoeuvres in Very Low Earth Orbit: Exploiting Lift for Short Warning Times and Reduced Orbital Decay
papers.summary: Very Low Earth Orbits (VLEO, below $450\,\mathrm{km}$ altitude) offer promising mission capabilities for future spacecraft, but increasing traffic and the presence of orbital debris create collision risks that pose a particular challenge for satellites without conventional propulsion. Aerodynamic drag, resulting from interaction with the residual atmosphere, has been shown effective for performing collision avoidance manoeuvres (CAMs). However, short warning times remain challenging, and current methods do not exploit aerodynamic lift forces that enable out-of-track manoeuvres, which could help enhance control authority and mitigate drag-induced orbital decay. This work addresses both gaps by developing and evaluating two complementary optimisation methods: a heuristic approach using reachable set analysis to determine minimum lead times, and a direct shooting method to limit the increase in orbital decay due to the manoeuvre. Analyses using data derived from real conjunctions show that achieving a sufficient reduction in collision risk in the considered scenarios is feasible with lead times lower than one orbital period. Results also show that lift-based manoeuvres outperform drag-only approaches, with modest lead time reductions and more pronounced benefits in limiting orbital decay. Performance sensitivity to variations in control authority due to the type of gas-surface-interaction, altitude, and the encounter geometry is characterised. The methods and results presented highlight the potential of aerodynamic CAM for short warning time scenarios, contributing to sustainable operations in the increasingly congested VLEO environment.
papers.title_ja: 超低軌道における気動学的衝突回避機動：短い警告時間と軌道減衰低減のための揚力活用
papers.summary_ja: 超低軌道（VLEO）における衛星の衝突回避機動（CAM）において、従来の抗力のみを用いる手法の限界を克服するため、揚力を活用した最適化手法を提案する。到達可能集合を用いたヒューリスティック手法と、軌道減衰を抑制するための直接射撃法を組み合わせ、短い警告時間下での機動可能性を評価した。実際の接近データを用いた解析により、1軌道周期未満のリードタイムで衝突リスクを低減できることを示し、揚力ベースの機動が抗力のみより軌道減衰の抑制に優れることを確認した。
papers.relevance_reason: 軌道力学と最適化手法の組み合わせであり、ユーザーの関心領域に直結する。

papers.title: CHORD: Learning Latent Spaces for Constrained Stellarator Design
papers.summary: In high-dimensional, PDE-constrained design, interpolating between known feasible solutions can reveal trade-offs without repeating expensive optimization campaigns. In stellarator design for fusion energy, direct interpolation of plasma boundary parameters can violate physical constraints even when both endpoints are feasible. Learned latent representations can capture nonlinear relationships among design variables, but latent interpolation can still cross infeasible regions, and conditioning on target metrics can become inconsistent with the decoded design. We introduce CHORD, a conditional variational autoencoder that penalizes predicted constraint violations along decoded latent interpolants during training, paired with self-consistent inference that aligns conditioning with the decoded design's predicted metrics. Geometric benchmarks show the benefit of regularizing latent interpolants. In stellarator interpolation between distinct geometry families, CHORD reaches up to 81% simulator-validated mid-segment feasibility, compared with 50% for an unregularized conditional VAE and 28% for direct interpolation of boundary parameters. Ablations show that both ingredients are needed for this gain. Beyond interpolation, latent-space optimization finds simulator-feasible designs, while self-consistent sampling produces more diverse feasible alternatives. On the ConStellaration benchmark, chord-regularized models with linear conditioning reuse data from five optimization campaigns and simulator-labeled rescalings to populate the Pareto front more densely. After low-fidelity screening, 93% of 1.2k generated candidates pass the benchmark's high-fidelity feasibility test. We release code and over 600k designs for stellarator generation, surrogate training, and front-filling evaluation. These results support feasibility-aware latent learning for exploring constrained design trade-offs.
papers.title_ja: CHORD: 制約付きステラレータ設計のための潜在空間学習
papers.summary_ja: CHORDは、条件付き変分オートエンコーダを用いて、ステラレータ（核融合炉）の設計変数間の非線形関係を潜在空間で捉える手法である。訓練時に潜在空間の補間経路上での制約違反をペナルティとして課し、推論時の条件付けと復号された設計指標の自己整合性を確保する。これにより、異なる幾何学族間の補間において、未正規化モデルや直接補間と比較して大幅に高い実効性（81%）を実現した。さらに、低忠実度スクリーニング後の高忠実度検証で93%の候補が合格し、Paretoフロンティアの高密度化にも寄与している。
papers.relevance_reason: サロゲートモデルと制約付き最適化の組み合わせが関心に合致

papers.title: HEAR, SEE, SPIKE ONCE: Highly Efficient NeuroAI Temporal Neural Networks for Low-Precision Multimodal Audio-Visual Classification and Online Learning
papers.summary: Spiking neural networks for multimodal audio-visual classification reach high accuracy by adopting deep-learning machinery: multi-stage convolutional or transformer encoders trained end-to-end with surrogate-gradient backpropagation through time. These prior works typically rely on full-precision (32-bit) parameters and do not treat hardware efficiency as a primary design objective. In this paper, we propose NeuTNN-AV, a much simpler hardware-amenable multimodal substrate built on the recently proposed NeuroAI Temporal Neural Network (NeuTNN) and demonstrate that it can match or outperform state-of-the-art SNN baselines with a fraction of their synapse counts. NeuTNN neurons carry multiple active dendritic segments. Each input line spikes at most once (temporal coding) and every weight is learned via a local reward-modulated spike-timing dependent plasticity (STDP) rule. All weights are 4-bit integers and inference uses only comparisons and additions. On CREMA-D, it reaches 78.6% with 2.34M synapses establishing a new state-of-the-art SNN accuracy, against 77.14% for MISNet-XL (31M parameters). On UrbanSound8K-AV, NeuTNN reaches 98.82% with 1.38M synapses, against 96.85% for SMMT (9.99M parameters) and 98.96% for MISNet-XL (31M parameters). Weight memory is 23-106x smaller than the spiking baselines, and the measured synaptic energy per inference is two to three orders of magnitude lower. Furthermore, the proposed NeuTNN learns CREMA-D in a single pass with 73.8% accuracy and demonstrates rapid online continual learning by adapting to unseen actors from a few dozen clips.
papers.title_ja: HEAR, SEE, SPIKE ONCE: 低精度マルチモーダル音声・視覚分類とオンライン学習のための高効率NeuroAI時間ニューラルネットワーク
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、スパイキングニューラルネットワーク（SNN）のハードウェア効率を大幅に向上させるNeuTNN-AVを提案する。4ビット整数重みと局所的なSTDP学習則を用いることで、推論時の演算を比較と加算のみで実現し、既存のSNNベースラインと比較してシナプス数を1/10〜1/100に削減しながら同等以上の精度を達成した。CREMA-DやUrbanSound8K-AVなどのマルチモーダルデータセットで、少ないパラメータ数ながらSOTA性能を示し、エネルギー効率の大幅な改善を実証している。さらに、単一パス学習やオンライン継続学習における適応能力も示しており、低電力環境での実用化に向けた重要な進展である。
papers.relevance_reason: LLM効率化・量子化・低精度推論の観点で高度に関連

papers.title: Metamorphic Testing of Learned Spatial Surrogates for Transit Accessibility
papers.summary: Transit-network design requires evaluating many candidates, but detailed accessibility calculations are too slow to repeat inside an optimization loop. We therefore train a neural surrogate to approximate them. Given a candidate bus network and fixed information about rail service and nearby opportunities, it predicts the calculated spatial change in accessibility. We compare its predictions with routing-derived targets in geographically held-out regions and test specified qualitative relations under controlled input changes. Reference calculations on constructed networks assess the applicability of relations that have a routing-level counterpart. Models with positive predictive skill can still fail basic connectivity tests. One targeted intervention substantially increases pass rates for two connectivity relations while predictive skill also improves. Average prediction error is therefore insufficient when a learned model becomes an optimization objective. Predictive agreement and controlled behavioral tests should be reported separately.
papers.title_ja: 交通アクセス性における学習済み空間サロゲートのメタモルフィックテスト

papers.title: DynaMimic: A Physics-Informed World Model for Humanoid Motion Tracking
papers.summary: Whole-body motion tracking enables humanoid robots to reproduce diverse skills from human demonstrations. Existing model-free reinforcement learning methods either distill motion specialists into a single policy at the cost of performance or train a generalist policy directly using cluster-scale computation. SuperMimic reduces this computational cost through a differentiable world model that implicitly learns the physics shared across motions by predicting the next state from the current state and action. However, this implicit formulation may not fully capture the underlying physical processes. Errors around changes of support can accumulate over imagined rollouts used to train the tracking policy. To address this challenge, we introduce DynaMimic, a differentiable world model that explicitly incorporates shared physics into state prediction. Specifically, its network predicts a contact wrench at each candidate support link and a residual generalized force. DynaMimic then uses these predictions to compute the next state through closed-form Lagrangian forward dynamics. Across 60 full LAFAN1 motions, DynaMimic reduces mean per-joint position error (MPJPE) by 18.6% relative to SuperMimic. For terrain tracking, we give both methods the same local height maps. Relative to terrain-conditioned SuperMimic, DynaMimic reduces MPJPE by 14.9% on A3 Parkour (66.15 to 56.28~mm) and by 10.8% on GRAIL terrain clips (141.88 to 126.57~mm). On a real A3 humanoid, the learned policies can perform diverse skills, such as floor recovery, cartwheel and a box vault.

papers.summary_ja: ヒューマノイドロボットの全身モーショントラッキングにおいて、既存の暗黙的なワールドモデルが持つ物理的誤差蓄積問題を解決する手法を提案する。本手法は、接触力と残差一般化力を予測し、ラグランジュ方程式による閉形式の前方ダイナミクス計算を明示的に組み込むことで、より正確な状態予測を実現する。LAFAN1データセットでの評価により、既存手法SuperMimicと比較して関節位置誤差を最大18.6%低減し、地形追従性能も向上させた。実機A3ヒューマノイドにおいても、床からの回復や箱越えなど多様なスキルを安定して実行できることを実証した。

papers.title: Bayesian Data Integration and Model Updating in Probabilistic Digital Twins
papers.summary: This paper proposes a framework for sequential Bayesian updating in probabilistic digital twins using data from multiple sources collected over time. The framework distinguishes between property data and behavior data, according to how observations relate to the digital state. Property data directly inform a subset of the uncertain model parameters and can therefore be incorporated using efficient dedicated Bayesian updating methods. Behavior data provide indirect information through the prediction model and require the solution of a Bayesian inverse problem. To reduce the associated computational cost, an active-learning-based surrogate strategy is introduced that evolves with the digital state and adaptively refines the prediction model in regions relevant to posterior inference. The framework is evaluated using an idealized cantilever beam example and a geotechnical case study of a canal wall subject to varying water levels and corrosion. The examples show how complementary data sources, including both equality observations and inequality information from observed system survival, can inform uncertain parameters and system reliability. The proposed surrogate-based updating scheme yields posterior estimates and prediction accuracy comparable to those of physics-based updating while requiring substantially fewer model evaluations. The proposed framework thus supports multi-source updating and reliability assessment in probabilistic digital twins of engineering systems.

papers.title: A Hybrid Analytical-Neural Residual Surrogate for Fast Radio Propagation Prediction over Irregular Terrain
papers.summary: Fast prediction of radio-wave propagation over irregular terrain is important for coverage analysis in mountainous environments, where many terrain and antenna configurations must be evaluated repeatedly. High-fidelity split-step parabolic equation (SSPE) solvers can capture terrain-induced shadowing and interference, but their computational cost is high for repeated planning studies. Learning-based surrogates reduce this cost, but direct field regression asks the network to learn both analytically tractable propagation trends and terrain-dependent residual structure. This paper proposes a hybrid analytical-neural residual surrogate that separates these two parts. A deterministic analytical baseline represents free-space spreading, antenna directivity, modified knife-edge diffraction, and terrain-aware specular reflection, while a compact coarse-to-fine neural network predicts the residual field. The network uses baseline-derived guidance channels, anisotropic convolutions, and feature-wise antenna conditioning to match the directional structure of terrain propagation fields. On synthetic SSPE data at 1.0 GHz, the proposed model achieves an MAE of 2.1061 dB, compared with 3.3955 dB for a standard U-Net and 3.2560 dB for a reproduced physics-guided CNN, while reducing the average inference time to 11.30 ms per sample. A zero-shot test at 1.8 GHz gives an MAE of 2.8692 dB without retraining, and a case study on the measured Hjorringvej terrain profile shows that the prediction remains consistent with the SSPE reference and follows the measured path-loss trend.
papers.title_ja: 不整地形における高速電波伝搬予測のためのハイブリッド解析・ニューラル残差サロゲート
papers.summary_ja: 不整地形での電波伝搬予測において、高忠実度だが計算コストの高いSSPEソルバーの代替として、解析的ベースラインとコンパクトなニューラルネットワークを組み合わせるハイブリッドサロゲートモデルを提案する。解析モデルが自由空間伝搬や回折などの基本的なトレンドを扱い、ネットワークが地形依存の残差構造を予測することで、学習負荷を軽減する。合成データでの実験では、標準的なU-Netや物理情報CNNと比較して平均絶対誤差（MAE）を大幅に低減し、推論時間を11.30msまで短縮した。さらに、周波数を変えたゼロショットテストや実測地形プロファイルを用いたケーススタディでも、SSPE参照値と整合する高精度な予測性能を示した。

papers.title: Data-driven Reduced-order Modeling of a Multistable Viscoelastic Flow
papers.summary: Viscoelastic flow past two side-by-side microcylinders has been shown to exhibit geometry-dependent transitions among symmetric, converging, diverging, and asymmetric-diverging flow states, together with regions of bistability and tristability. Here, we develop a data-driven framework for learning a two-dimensional, parameter-dependent normal form for this bifurcation structure from sparse measurements of stable flow states. We use the flow asymmetry parameters $I'$ and $I''$ as state variables, with the gap ratio $G$ and Weissenberg number $Wi$ as control parameters. In the absence of trajectory data, the measured steady states are enforced as stable equilibria of the learned vector field through equilibrium and local-stability constraints. We examine both polynomial and neural-network representations of the associated normal form and incorporate the physical reflection symmetry directly into the model. The resulting models recover the main geometry-dependent transitions and the overall structure of the experimental phase diagram. To reduce additional stable equilibria that are not constrained by the measurements, we introduce an iterative negative-sample procedure that refines the predicted equilibrium structure. Combining equilibrium data, local stability, physical symmetry, and negative samples yields the closest agreement with the experimental phase diagram among the models considered. The remaining discrepancies reflect the limited information available, solely in the form of sparse equilibrium measurements. Overall, the framework aims to showcase a prototypical example of both the potential and the limitations of inferring nonlinear flow dynamics from sparse equilibrium measurements and highlight the importance of physical constraints and additional dynamical information for reconstructing complex bifurcation structures.

papers.title: Theory-Informed Quantum Error Mitigation for Shor Order Finding with Fourier Neural Operators
papers.summary: Quantum noise distorts the distribution of circuit measurement outcomes, often leaving enough information to infer the algorithm's correct result. To recover this latent information from the noisy distribution in Shor order finding, we introduce a theory-informed quantum error mitigation method. We model how circuit errors shift, broaden, or weaken peaks in the output distribution. These models guide both the generation of synthetic training data and the design of a Fourier neural operator with a learned gain that attenuates or amplifies higher retained Fourier modes. We score each candidate order by averaging the correlations between its ideal distribution and the distributions measured in three circuit executions. The network adjusts these scores to guide the order estimate and determine the weights of a normalized mixture of the ideal distributions. On 1,351 simulated test cases for general modular exponentiation, held out by circuit configuration, exact order recovery rises from 19% to 34%, and the median Jensen-Shannon divergence from the ideal distribution falls by 50%, from 0.64 to 0.32. On 101 Mersenne rotation circuits executed across five IBM quantum processors, a separate model trained and calibrated in simulation increases the number of correct order estimates from 35 to 53. Algorithmic structure can remain recoverable even when noise makes it barely visible.
papers.title_ja: Fourier ニューラルオペレータを用いた理論情報に基づく Shor 順序発見の量子誤り緩和
papers.summary_ja: Shor アルゴリズムにおける量子ノイズによる出力分布の歪みを理論的にモデル化し、Fourier ニューラルオペレータ（FNO）を用いた誤り緩和手法を提案する。回路エラーがピークに与える影響を学習データ生成とネットワーク設計に反映させ、理想分布との相関スコアを調整して正確な順序推定を行う。シミュレーションでは正確な順序復元率が 19% から 34% に向上し、IBM 量子プロセッサの実機実験でも正解数が 35 から 53 に増加した。

papers.title: Quantum kernels on breast data: concentration, surrogates, and two ways an advantage gets manufactured
papers.summary: Quantum-kernel advantage claims on breast data are usually a single number: one quantum arm, one comparator, one test split. We asked what that number measures once the full comparator set and selection history are visible. We report three active benchmarks, all exact classical statevector simulations of 8-qubit fidelity kernels with no quantum component in the inference path: a sample-efficiency sweep on Wisconsin Diagnostic Breast Cancer at ten training-set sizes; raw-versus-processed arms on 1,200 M-SYNTH simulated mammograms with a matched closed-form dequantisation surrogate, five classical methods at the same input and eleven kernel families; and a 30-seed selection-inflation measurement on BreastMNIST. A CMMD D1 clinical arm is withdrawn as a result arm because its frozen splits leak the label through patient serial order, a defect reported in a separate study; it is retained only as a worked example. All three active arms are negative. On M-SYNTH raw an apparent +0.1736 (p = 5.2e-06) against a tuned RBF-SVM falls to +0.0019 (p = 0.937) against a random forest at the same input, and a Laplacian kernel wins on validation. On WDBC, with model selection confined to training data, the quantum kernel is below the selected classical arm at every training-set size, with 2 of 200 paired subsamples ahead. Best-of-30 seed selection adds +0.0210 on BreastMNIST. One result does not fit: at bandwidth 2pi the matched closed-form Gaussian surrogate failed to reproduce the M-SYNTH raw kernel (0.5410 against 0.7045, p = 6.3e-06). Comparator choice and selection each produce effects larger than any quantum-classical difference we measured; we give a reporting standard that removes both.
papers.title_ja: 乳腺データにおける量子カーネル：集中度、サロゲート、そして優位性が製造される2つの経路
papers.summary_ja: 本研究は、乳腺がんデータにおける量子カーネルの優位性主張が、比較対象の選択やモデル選定プロセスによって歪められていることを示す。8量子ビットの忠実度カーネルを古典的にシミュレートし、WDBC、M-SYNTH、BreastMNISTの3つのベンチマークで評価した結果、いずれも量子カーネルは同等の古典的手法（ランダムフォレストやラプラシアンカーネルなど）に劣る、または同等であることが判明した。特に、比較対象の選択やシード選定によるインフレーション効果が、量子と古典の性能差よりも大きいことを定量的に示した。また、閉形式ガウスサロゲートモデルが特定の帯域幅で量子カーネルを再現できなかったという興味深い不一致も報告されている。

papers.title: Neural-operator acceleration of bidirectional phonon Boltzmann-Fourier coupling for multiscale heat transport in silicon fin arrays
papers.summary: Localized heating in semiconductor devices can produce non-diffusive phonon transport near heat-generating regions, while heat spreading through the surrounding substrate remains well described by Fourier conduction. We present a hybrid framework that couples a pretrained neural operator for the phonon Boltzmann transport equation (BTE) within individual fins to a Fourier model of a shared substrate. To reduce the cost of repeated BTE solves across fin positions and coupling iterations, a DeepONet maps each fin's substrate-interface temperature and heating state to its temperature and heat-flux fields. The operator is trained on interface temperatures generated by a linearized proxy of the coupled problem, which avoids explicit training data collection from full coupled runs. An energy-balance penalty regularizes the learned operator, and a mixed finite-element formulation represents substrate heat flux in an H(div)-conforming space. The two models exchange temperature and normal heat flux through a non-overlapping Schwarz iteration with adaptive Aitken relaxation. We evaluate the framework on an idealized three-dimensional array of 100 silicon fins. For a held-out switching configuration, the neural-operator-Fourier solution differs from the direct BTE-Fourier reference by a maximum of 0.3 K in temperature and 0.6% in relative flux across all fins. Excluding the one-time substrate factorization, the coupled surrogate run takes about 50 s, compared with 2 h 28 min for direct coupling, a speedup of approximately 180x. Additional held-out switching patterns converge with the same trained operator. These results demonstrate neural-operator acceleration of bidirectional kinetic-continuum coupling for the tested geometry and material. This bidirectional strategy may extend to other multiscale materials problems coupling learned local neural models with continuum solvers.

papers.title: Uncertainty Quantification and Global Sensitivity Analysis of Patient-Specific Coronary Hemodynamics Under Unsteady Flow Conditions
papers.summary: Patient-specific computational models of the coronary arteries demonstrate transformative potential for physiological assessment, identifying hemodynamic markers associated with disease progression, and optimizing treatment. Unfortunately, these models rarely account for input parameter uncertainty, limiting confidence in predictions and their clinical interpretation. Herein, we present a novel uncertainty quantification-finite element framework that integrates computationally efficient techniques to characterize and propagate uncertainty through patient-specific coronary simulations under unsteady flow conditions. Principal component analysis characterized variability in pulsatile coronary velocity waveforms, while uncertainty in blood pressure, viscosity, density, and heart rate is represented through probability distributions. Polynomial chaos expansion (PCE) enabled efficient uncertainty propagation and global sensitivity analysis across three patient-specific models, quantifying variability in time-averaged wall shear stress (WSS), oscillatory shear index, and cross-flow index. Fourth-order PCE emulators converged across all three patients, yielding analyses of 505 models per patient, with median coefficients of variation ranging from 0.15-0.20 for time-averaged WSS, 0.54-0.75 for oscillatory shear index, and 0.28-0.38 for cross-flow index, highlighting greater relative uncertainty in multidirectional WSS metrics. Global sensitivity analysis revealed that time-averaged WSS variability was governed by the individual effects of velocity and blood viscosity, with parameter interactions contributing <2% of total variance. In contrast, velocity waveform uncertainty dominated variability in the oscillatory shear index and cross-flow index, with higher-order parameter interactions accounting for 20.7-34.5% and 26.6-37.8% of total variance, respectively.

papers.title: Three-Dimensional Wake Reconstruction and Cross-Scale Transfer for Floating Offshore Wind Turbines via Physics-Informed Fourier Neural Operators
papers.summary: Coupled surge-pitch motions drive unsteady vortex interactions and dynamic wake meandering behind floating offshore wind turbines, complicating three-dimensional wake reconstruction from limited measurements and transfer across turbine scales. Large-eddy simulations coupled with an actuator line model generate fixed and surge-pitch wakes at motion-based Strouhal numbers $St=fD/U_\infty$ of 0.2-0.6 (where $f$, $D$, and $U_\infty$ are the motion frequency, rotor diameter, and inflow velocity) for the National Renewable Energy Laboratory 5 MW ($D=126$ m) and International Energy Agency 22 MW ($D=284$ m) turbines. A physics-informed Fourier neural operator framework combines four-dimensional spectral convolutions with incompressible continuity and rotor-forced momentum-residual regularization to reconstruct three-dimensional unsteady wakes from two observation planes. Trained on the 5 MW fixed and $St=0.2$-$0.5$ cases, the framework recovers near-wake double-peak deficits, motion-driven wake expansion, and coherent vortices through $St=0.6$ (mean wake-center and half-width errors within 1.3% and 1.0% of $D$), while 10% planar sampling preserves near-dense accuracy (relative $L_2$ error 0.0689 versus 0.0684). Applying transfer learning from the 5 MW to the 22 MW turbine lowers the three-dimensional streamwise-velocity error at $St=0.6$ by 36% relative to zero-shot inference (0.1066 to 0.0682), halves scratch-training error with one fixed case (0.0835 versus 0.1693), and restores wake-center tracking and motion-locked harmonics ($St$-$3St$). Large-scale motion-induced dynamics transfer cleanly across turbine scales, whereas fine-scale vortex breakdown remains damped. The framework shows potential for three-dimensional wake reconstruction and downstream-inflow assessment in floating wind farms.

papers.title: DED-Agent: An agentic AI method for autonomous thermal simulation model development and calibration in laser directed energy deposition
papers.summary: In metal additive manufacturing (AM), process parameters set the local thermal history, which governs defects, microstructure and properties. Laser power, scan speed, hatch spacing, layer thickness, scan strategy and position combine into a design space of 10^4-10^6 conditions, which is beyond what human experts can map by hand with finite element (FE) thermal models: every model must be set up, meshed, solved and calibrated by an expert, and calibrating unknown heat-source parameters alone can take days to weeks. This paper presents DED-Agent, an agentic artificial intelligence (AI) method for autonomous simulation model development and calibration in laser directed energy deposition (L-DED). A supervisor agent coordinates three specialist agents that share a structured simulation specification and call open-source tools. An intent agent turns a plain-language request into a validated specification, a simulation agent builds, runs and checks an FE thermal model through physics-aware step-by-step reasoning, and a calibration agent identifies key heat-source parameters against experimental data (e.g., thermocouple data) using a high-order proper generalized decomposition (HOPGD) surrogate within a trust-region search. On five benchmark builds, from single-track walls to a multi-track band on a cylindrical tube, the agents built executable thermal models without manual intervention, with 4.1-9.1% error for the simple and medium builds. Within three calibration rounds, the error fell to 0.9-2.5%. The surrogate matched full FE to within 0.08-1.55% and shortened calibration by 5-13 times. Agentic AI can thus autonomously establish reliable, accurate simulation models for AM processes and accelerate the search for process parameters that control microstructure.
