papers.title: Conservative Overlap Fuzzy Rough Sets for Incomplete Data
papers.summary: Attribute reduction in incomplete information systems is difficult because missing values break the equivalence-class structure of rough set theory. We propose the Conservative Overlap Fuzzy Rough Set (COFRS) model. Each object is described by its set of present attributes. The similarity of two objects is a weighted overlap on the attributes present in both, divided by the fixed number of attributes |A| instead of the size of their union, so missing values are penalised globally and are not matched as wildcards. From this similarity we define a soft dependency degree based on weighted granule consistency, and we search for reducts by greedy backward elimination in O(|U|^2 |A|^2) time. We show that the relation is symmetric and non-reflexive, that the dependency degree is not monotone, and we give a sufficient condition under which monotonicity holds. On 11 UCI benchmarks with missing rates from 0.15% to 20.46%, COFRS gives the smallest reducts on average (4.1 attributes, against 5.0-11.2 for Tolerance-RS, a range-threshold variant Tol-RS_tau, Zhou-RS and the min-aggregation variant COFRS-min). The difference is significant against Tol-RS_tau, Zhou-RS and COFRS-min (Holm-adjusted Wilcoxon p<0.01) but not against Tolerance-RS (p=0.56), and it is small against the Jensen-Shen selector (adjusted p=0.084). At equal reduct size, COFRS selects more informative attributes than random subsets. With a kNN classifier the methods do not differ significantly in accuracy, F1 or G-mean; with an RBF-SVM they do, and COFRS ranks last. The gain is therefore compactness, not predictive accuracy.
papers.title_ja: 不完全データのための保守的重なりファジ粗集合
papers.summary_ja: 不完全情報システムにおける属性削減問題を解決するため、欠損値をグローバルにペナルティ化するCOFRSモデルを提案する。既存手法と比較し、UCIベンチマーク上で平均的に最もコンパクトな還元集合（4.1属性）を生成することを示した。ただし予測精度の向上は限定的であり、主な利点はモデルの簡潔さ（コンパクトネス）にある。
papers.relevance_reason: 粗集合理論の応用であり、LLMや軌道力学との直接的な関連は薄い

papers.title: An Automated Framework Integrating Deep Learning and Anatomical Reasoning for Cardiac Phenotyping From CCTA
papers.summary: Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) depicts coronary anatomy and cardiac fat, but segmentation alone does not ensure anatomically consistent measurements. We propose an automated framework that combines deep learning with anatomical reasoning for quantitative cardiac phenotyping. Its anatomical measurement module uses graph geometry, branch identity, and surrounding structures to define vessel-specific pericoronary adipose tissue (PCAT) sampling and a surrogate epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) compartment. The latter also generates training targets without requiring expert pericardium contours. A companion module quantifies coronary calcium on non-contrast CT. Component-wise benchmarking was conducted on five public datasets: ImageCAS, ImageCAS-X, COCA, Visual Lab, and MultiD4CAD. On ImageCAS-X Test-160, lumen segmentation with validation-selected post-processing achieved a Dice score of 0.9133 and a clDice score of 0.940, exceeding the corresponding published CAS-Net point estimates. In the four-split ImageCAS evaluation, the four-member ensemble outperformed the single ResEnc-L model. Analysis of 800 paired scans showed that PCAT attenuation measurements differed between whole-vessel and lumen references. External EAT evaluation showed strong volume correlation and good spatial overlap. Explicit anatomical rules make the resulting measurements interpretable and inspectable. In practice, the framework provides a standardized pipeline for processing cardiac CT cohorts and quantifying coronary calcium, PCAT, and EAT for population-level analysis and comparison across studies. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/HarryTRAN207/CardiacCT-Research
papers.title_ja: CCTAからの心臓フェノタイピングのための深層学習と解剖学的推論を統合した自動化フレームワーク
papers.summary_ja: 冠動脈CT血管造影（CCTA）の定量解析において、単なるセグメンテーションでは解剖学的整合性が担保されない問題を解決するため、深層学習と解剖学的ルールを統合した自動化フレームワークを提案する。グラフ幾何学や枝の同一性を用いた血管特異的な冠周囲脂肪組織（PCAT）サンプリング、および専門家アノテーション不要の心外膜脂肪組織（EAT）サロゲート区画の生成を実現した。5つの公開データセットでのベンチマークにより、既存手法を上回るセグメンテーション精度と、PCAT測定値の解釈可能性・再現性を示した。

papers.title: Directed brain-body graphs across timescales
papers.summary: Simultaneous brain and body recordings combine signals sampled at very different rates with processes that act on timescales from milliseconds to minutes. Placing all signals on one time grid can distort the directed relationships estimated from them. Unmeasured common influences can also make one signal appear to drive another. We introduce rate-matched Granger causality (RMGC), which estimates directed predictive relationships without a common sampling grid. Each relationship receives a robustness value, the strength of the weakest common influence found within a specified class that can reproduce it. A neural extension tests for nonlinear relationships. In a controlled benchmark, RMGC recovered more true relationships than four established methods and an autoregressive model on a common grid (92\% at a false-positive rate of 5\%). Given the same signal features, the common-grid model matched this recovery but had more than twice the false-positive rate, and it reversed the relationship from respiration to heart rate. The robustness value never overstated the strength of the driver behind a spurious relationship, even for drivers outside the searched class. It separated true from spurious relationships better than predictive strength did. In overnight sleep recordings and two awake datasets, many brain--heart relationships could be reproduced by common drivers no stronger than measured respiration. Robustness values only partly identified those that appeared when respiration was omitted, particularly during wakefulness. Surrogate analyses showed elevated background rates in one awake dataset. The approach applies to other signals recorded at different rates or as events, provided that influences act with a delay.
papers.title_ja: 時間スケールを超えた脳-身体間の有向グラフ
papers.summary_ja: 異なるサンプリングレートで記録された脳と身体の信号間の因果関係を推定する新しい手法「レートマッチング・グレンジャー因果性（RMGC）」を提案する。共通の時間グリッドに揃えることによる歪みを避け、測定されていない共通要因による偽の因果関係に対する頑健性値を算出する。ベンチマークでは既存手法より真の関係を多く検出でき、偽陽性率を低減した。睡眠中の脳-心臓関係の多くが呼吸などの共通要因で説明可能であることを示し、非線形関係の検出にも対応する。

papers.title: ToneMamaba: Learning Contextualized Tonal Contours with Boundary-Reset State Space Models
papers.summary: Mandarin tone recognition in connected speech is challenging because contextual and durational variation reshapes F0 contours. We propose ToneMamba, a boundary-aware state space model that replaces static boundary embeddings with bidirectional state resets at syllable, word, and IPU levels. Fixed weights fuse multi-level representations, while shared-weight bidirectional scans use channel-wise directional fusion to reduce parameters. Dynamic syllable pooling forms tonal contours, and rhythm-conditioned gating incorporates durational information. ToneMamba achieves 97.9% and 74.8% accuracy on FCU-VOICE-360 read and MCDC-8 conversational speech, outperforming the baseline (ToneNet) by 0.9 and 15.9 percentage points, respectively. Ablations show that word-level resets are particularly effective, while rhythm conditioning provides greater gains in conversational speech, underscoring the role of durational variation in spontaneous speech.
papers.title_ja: ToneMamaba: 境界リセット状態空間モデルによる文脈依存トーン輪郭の学習
papers.summary_ja: 連続話法における中国語のトーン認識において、文脈や時間的変動によるF0輪郭の変化を扱うための境界認識型状態空間モデル（SSM）を提案する。静的な境界埋め込みの代わりに、音節・単語・IPUレベルでの双方向状態リセットを用い、固定重みによる多層表現融合と共有重みの双方向スキャンによりパラメータ数を削減する。リズム条件付きゲーティングにより時間情報を取り込み、FCU-VOICE-360およびMCDC-8データセットでベースラインを上回る高精度を達成した。

papers.title: The Jupiter ICy moons Explorer (JUICE) Mission: Post-Launch Status and Mission Overview
papers.summary: The JUpiter ICy Moons Explorer (JUICE) is the first large-class mission in ESA's Cosmic Vision programme. Proposed in 2007 and selected in 2012, it was launched on 14 April 2023 from Kourou and is now en route towards Jupiter. After arrival in July 2031, JUICE will spend approximately four years studying the Jupiter system, performing multiple flybys of three of its Galilean moons, the icy moons Ganymede, Europa, and Callisto, before entering orbit around Ganymede for its final year. The mission will investigate conditions that may support habitable environments within the satellites, all of which are thought to contain subsurface liquid water oceans. Ganymede, the largest moon in the Solar System, is a prime target due to its internal structure and possible subsurface ocean, its unique intrinsic magnetic field, and its complex interactions with Jupiter's magnetosphere, offering a natural laboratory for studying the emergence, evolution and potential habitability of icy worlds around giant planets. JUICE will also conduct a global investigation of the Jupiter system as the archetype for gaseous giant planet systems: it will study Jupiter's atmospheric circulation, composition, and flow of energy from the cloud tops to the thermosphere and characterise the 3D structure of the magnetosphere and its coupling with the ionosphere and thermosphere. Interactions between the moons and the magnetosphere, as well as tidal and gravitational evolution within the Galilean system, will also be assessed. Additional science objectives include the innermost Galilean moon, Io and its neutral cloud and plasma torus, some small inner and irregular moons, and the ring systems. The payload includes 10 instruments and one experiment using the spacecraft's telecommunications system to connect with ground-based radio telescopes, plus an onboard radiation monitor.
papers.title_ja: 木星氷衛星探査機（JUICE）ミッション：打上げ後の状況とミッション概要

papers.title: Realization of expanding dynamics by a finite horizon parabolic law response
papers.summary: We study the discrete dynamical system generated by iterating an episodic response of a population density. In each episode, the running potential is frozen at the current density, agents solve a quadratic control problem, and the terminal density is passed to the next episode. For each prescribed positive horizon $\tau$ and each $C^k$ map $F$ of finitely many Fourier moments, with $1\le k<\infty$, we construct a finite mode interaction realizing $F$ at order $\varepsilon$. In scaled coordinates, the exact parabolic response satisfies $\|T^{(d)}_{\varepsilon,\tau}-(F,S(\tau)|_{\Es_d})\|_{C^k}\le C\varepsilon$. The estimate is uniform over a full bounded infinite dimensional Sobolev fibre and needs neither Fourier truncation nor an invariant manifold. For scalar targets with disjoint expanding branches that strictly cover their convex hull, this $C^1$ control and parabolic compactness yield compact invariant sets of the exact response. These sets factor onto the full one sided shift and contain periodic densities of every least period. Nondegenerate periodic orbits continue, and hyperbolicity requires a separate strict multiplier condition. We also prove a derivative cost obstruction for nonaffine microscopic realization, a susceptibility weighted criterion for population energy designs, and the failure of exact scalar closure under nontrivial rank one feedback. The results concern designed frozen law responses, not Nash consistent mean field game equilibria or finite player limits.

papers.title: The W Transform: an additional powerful tool for astrophysical time-series analysis
papers.summary: This work introduces the W Transform (WT) for astrophysical applications and explores its similarities and differences to the Continuous Wavelet Transform (CWT), in photometric stellar light curves (LCs). We tested both techniques on synthetic data, producing LCs with different noise levels and numbers of gaps, and applied them to LCs from TESS space mission. The analysis focused on six stars: the solar analog TIC 276293046, the ultra-cool dwarf TIC 359892714, the $\gamma$ Dor pulsator TIC 164173105, the eclipsing binary TIC 355151781, the hosting planet star TIC 142276270, and the brown dwarf TIC 102076870. Overall, the results were in agreement, except for stars with LCs presenting sector-to-sector differences in structures or changes in the number of gaps, reflecting time-dynamic effects in the same target, which affect how time-dependent variability features appear in the time-frequency representation. For such LCs, the WT spectra are more stable and accurate in recovering signal amplitudes than the CWT maps, which exhibit distortions and limitations, showing that the inherent flexibility of the WT method in adjusting the dominant frequency could enhance time resolution even in LCs with complex or variable structures. We conclude that the WT is a robust tool for the analysis of stellar LCs, and that both methods may complement each other in an in-depth analysis of a periodic astrophysical signal. The present results suggest that the WT is a robust and accurate tool for analyzing stellar LCs, expanding the range of numerical techniques available for analyzing different stellar periodic phenomena from photometric observations.

papers.title: Whistler instability driven by electron trapping in magnetic dips
papers.summary: Using fully kinetic particle-in-cell simulations, we show how free energy released by an ion-scale instability reaches electron scales through its effect on the electron distribution. An initial ion temperature anisotropy drives partly compressional ion cyclotron waves, which form magnetic dips. Electrons trapped in these dips develop an enhanced temperature anisotropy and butterfly-shaped distributions, similar to those observed by spacecraft in the Earth's magnetosheath. By tracking the energy transfer in velocity space, we show that the gradients created by trapping drive whistler waves through cyclotron resonance. The whistlers in turn scatter the electrons in pitch angle, flattening velocity-space gradients and heating the electrons along the magnetic field. As a result, the electron anisotropy drops to about half of the double-adiabatic prediction once the whistler power peaks. Our results show that it is the shape of the electron distribution in magnetic dips, rather than its temperature anisotropy alone, that drives the whistlers.

papers.title: High-order polynomial corrections for embedded curved boundaries in discontinuous Galerkin methods for hyperbolic systems: from staircase instabilities to a gap method
papers.summary: High order polynomial corrections, which impose the boundary conditions on an embedded boundary by modifying the polynomial of the surrogate boundary cells, give accurate and robust discretizations of elliptic problems on unfitted meshes. We show that, used out of the box in discontinuous Galerkin discretizations of hyperbolic systems on Cartesian meshes, the shifted boundary and minimization-based (ROD) corrections become unstable, with eigenvalues of positive real part that no restriction of the time step can remove. Linear advection, whose operator is block triangular, is the least affected case: a tilted straight boundary makes every correction unstable with the geometry-normal map, while the face-orthogonal map, which likely gives a one-dimensional character to the boundary condition with tensor-product bases, keeps the 1D stability up to one polynomial degree less. The slip wall of the linear acoustic system is much more critical: all the corrections are unstable already on a tilted straight wall, and an energy balance shows that the cause is the misalignment, in direction and in position, between the faces of the staircase and the wall. Since the origin of the instability is geometric, we act on the surrogate boundary itself, and develop the gap paradigm for discontinuous Galerkin discretizations of hyperbolic systems: each boundary cell is extended, by extrapolating its polynomial without new degrees of freedom, up to the segments joining the projections of its vertices on the wall, where the boundary condition is imposed, and neighbouring extended cells exchange information through the numerical fluxes used on the interior interfaces. Numerical experiments confirm the energy stability of the gap method on a straight wall and show high order convergence on curved walls, in configurations where the classical corrections applied on the staircase diverge.
